items.title: Josiah "Cie" Frazier Interview
items.q: I think in the year of 1950, Johnny Papacelestand's Jazz Band. I worked in there from 50 to 52.

ctx.x: Yeah, I don't remember that he told us about that particular group.

Yeah, yeah. I'm trying to think now. Who would I want in with after that? We played around here, 45 and let's see. I was doing field work then and working doing Days of Work. And I think in the year of 1950, Johnny Papacelestand's Jazz Band. I worked in there from 50 to 52. The 90s of Papacelestand, New Orleans Jazz Band. I played with him. When I left in that outfit, we went. Then I started working different field work with Poissy Humphrey. And then we started playing and we formally took that outfit and went…
How many years have you been with Emma now?

items.title: Josiah 'Cie' Frazier Interview, 1961-02-16
items.q: I went in the band 1951 or something like that, or 50, I think it was 1951. Oh, man. And I joined his band. And I played with him a good while.

ctx.x: Did you find yourself okay in that band?

Same, it's like, you didn't change from that same thing, you know, just want to have more men, you understand. Yeah, just more men, just like when I come out of the Navy band, the first, not a recording, but the first concert we played at the St. Charles Hotel was with Bunk Johnson and the George Lewis band, yeah. First night that you came in town, yeah, same trouble, baby, baby, baby, the doctor didn't come down, yeah. Oh. And they just come from making a tour in New York. I went to play, went to St. Charles…
Louis made a record with him, didn't he, with that, with that same band?

items.title: Josiah 'Cie' Frazier Interview, 1972-01-19
items.q: That's when I played that season with the Tuxedo Band. I'll give you the members of that band. Yeah, yeah. Well that band at that time consisted of, first had Bill Matthew on trombone, and Papa Celeste on cornet, and Rick High Lexie on cornet, two cornets.

ctx.x: That was the Young Morgan Band. Well, they called it Sam Morgan Band. Sam Morgan Band. Sam Morgan Band. But, say, Sammy got the best go year. You know, Johnny Day, I picked him right now, standing on Seminole in Claiborne waiting to catch the North Claiborne called the Ride Up Canal Street. Yeah. Well, that same year you're speaking about was John Morrell had got several fellas out there in the tuxedo band to make that record. I see. And he had wanted, Chani Bebe was the drummer, you see, but he was a crack…
So Paul Barch wasn't doing that band anymore then? Who? Paul Barch was gone. Oh no, no. He was up in New York that time.

items.title: Josiah "Cie" Frazier Interview, 1961-02-02
items.q: He played with the Tuxedo Band years ago. What, Celestan's Tuxedo Band? Celestan's Baby Ridgely.

ctx.x: Do you remember what he played like? Was he a good drummer?
He was not a good drummer. He played with the Tuxedo Band years ago. What, Celestan's Tuxedo Band? Celestan's Baby Ridgely.
